source.title: Scaling laws for post-training quantized large language models
source.authors: Zifei Xu; Alexander Lan; W. Yazar; Tristan Webb; Sayeh Sharify; Xin Wang

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It measures validation NLL against parameter count for pretrained language models, directly testing the parameter-scaling part of V1 on model families. It does not vary training tokens or compute.
record.gate_note: The paper also studies post-training quantization and a random-forest predictor. Those results concern quantized-model loss and its prediction, not power-law extrapolation of pretrained loss or compute-optimal allocation; the predictor findings are recorded under fits_no_version. Figure-only pretraining-loss values are retained per plotted model, not numerically estimated.
record.test_reason: Section 2.1 and Figure 1 (left) plot held-out WikiText-2 NLL against transformer weight parameter count for 18 off-the-shelf pretrained models from five families. The authors state that GPT-2, OPT and BLOOM 'roughly follow one power law' and that Llama 2/3 track a different path. This bears on the parameter part of V1. It is T2 rather than T1 because it compares released models with differing data and token budgets rather than running a controlled sweep. It is a thin check: there is no fitted exponent, no numbers, and the range is about two orders of magnitude (about 124M to 13B). The paper's main subject, post-training quantization loss, fits no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that post-training quantization outcomes are predictable from scaling of the local loss landscape, data formats and PTQ effects, via a random-forest model that generalizes to unseen families. They also present a Pareto frontier trading model size against quantization precision. They note validation only up to 13B parameters. The pretrained power law is recapitulated as background, not as a main finding.
record.recipe_differences: Measures held-out NLL against model parameter count, but uses already pretrained models from several families and does not vary training tokens or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed pretrained-loss path differs by model family. Quantized-loss outcomes vary with quantization format, model size and PTQ procedure; the paper also reports dataset-dependent experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: A random-forest regressor using parameter count, pretrained NLL, RTN SQNR/NLL, local loss slope and format features predicts post-GPTQ NLL reasonably well for held-out pythia-1b and mpt-7b. It also predicts across the C4 and LAMBADA datasets (Appendix F).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-training quantization loss of LLMs can be predicted from model, loss-landscape and format features across unseen model families and datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Within a family, larger models have flatter local radial loss landscapes (except OPT, per Figure 2 right). SQNR for MX formats is roughly invariant across models, while quantized NLL is nonlinear and less predictable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The local loss landscape flattens with model size, and post-training quantization loss follows family-specific, landscape-dependent trends rather than a simple power law.

record.peer_reviewed: 4th NeurIPS Efficient Natural Language and Speech Processing Workshop (ENLSP-IV 2024)
record.problems: Pretrained-loss values are presented graphically without numerical values in the text. The authors state that experiments cover models only up to 13 billion parameters and that prediction at much larger scales remains unvalidated. The V1 evidence uses pretrained models from different families rather than a controlled training sweep.
record.rows_left_out: No additional V1 model rows were omitted. Other quantization-format and GPTQ comparisons are not individually transcribed because they concern post-training quantization outcomes rather than the tested pretrained-loss scaling version.

untested.parts: Scaling with training tokens or compute; the condition that other factors are not the bottleneck; any fitted exponent or quantitative goodness of fit.
All: no fit on small runs is extrapolated to larger runs.
All: shape is not varied at fixed parameter count.
All: post-training quantization is neither a modality nor a listed training regime, and no power-law form is fitted to quantized loss.
All: no downstream tasks are measured.
No exponents are fitted or compared. The family offset hints at dependence on training setup but is not analysed.

record.verdict_notes: The V1 evidence is a single figure of released models with no numbers and no fitted exponent. Parameter count is the transformer-layer weight count, close to Kaplan's non-embedding convention. GPT-2, OPT and BLOOM differ in training data yet are said to share one curve, so the support is loose. Rows r1–r15 are acceptable as observed only in the authors' 'roughly' sense. Researchers should weight this study lightly for V1.

versions.untested_parts: The study varies parameter count only; it does not test scaling with training tokens or compute, or establish that other factors are not bottlenecks.
It does not test power laws fitted on small pretrained runs predicting the held-out loss of much larger pretrained runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token split is tested.
Architecture details are not varied while holding parameter count fixed.
The study examines post-training quantization of text models, but does not test whether the same power-law form holds across other modalities or the listed training regimes.
It does not estimate or compare scaling exponents across fitting choices, or test compute-optimal splits or curve bending.

source_check.notes: Individual NLL values remain figure only; the text supplies qualitative family-level conclusions. Parameter counts refer to transformer-layer weight tensors; training-token and compute effects are not independently tested.

statements.correction: Section 2.1: GPT-2, OPT and BLOOM approximately share a power law; Llama 2/3 follow a different, qualitatively similar path; no Llama power-law fit or departure from power-law form is established.
statements.problem: The different Llama parameter-loss path is accurately reported, but calling it a scope limit on V1 overstates the evidence: V1 does not require identical curves across families.
